lesson.title: Gap Trading: When the Market Jumps (or Falls) Overnight
lesson.content:
**What Happened This Morning — And Why It's a Perfect Lesson**

When you checked the market this morning, it opened LOWER than where it closed on Friday. That's called a **gap down** — and today is a perfect real-world example of one of the most important concepts in day trading.

**What Is a Gap?**

A gap happens when a stock or index opens at a noticeably different price from where it closed the day before. There are two kinds:

🔴 **Gap Down** — Opens lower than the previous close. Like today. The US Navy seized an Iranian ship over the weekend → Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz → oil prices jumped → markets opened lower Monday morning. The market "caught up" to bad news.

🟢 **Gap Up** — Opens higher. Common after a great earnings report or positive announcement released after the market closed.

**Why Do Gaps Happen?**

The stock market is closed on weekends and overnight. But news doesn't stop. When the market reopens, it adjusts instantly to everything that happened while it was closed. That instant adjustment IS the gap.

**The Two Classic Gap Trading Strategies**

**Strategy 1: Gap and Go (Ride the Momentum)**
If a stock gaps in a strong direction on powerful news and keeps moving that way after the open, some traders buy into the momentum. The idea: the news is so significant the move will continue all day.

Today's example: Energy stocks gapped up at the open because oil surged 6%. A Gap and Go trader might buy into oil-related stocks expecting the move to continue as long as Iran news stays tense.

**Strategy 2: Gap Fill (Play the Reversal)**
Here's a stat that surprises most beginners: roughly 70% of gaps eventually "fill" — meaning prices return to where they were before the gap happened. This is called the gap fill.

The theory: gaps are often emotional overreactions. Markets panic or get euphoric, then calm down and prices drift back to where they were.

Today's example: The S&P 500 gapped down from 7,126 to 7,110 this morning. A gap fill trade means watching for the market to stabilize around 10-11am, then buying expecting prices to drift back toward 7,126 by afternoon — IF Iran news doesn't get worse.

**How to Tell a Strong Gap from a Weak One**

Not all gaps are worth trading. Ask yourself:
- Is there **real, significant news** behind this gap, or just noise?
- Is **volume surging** to confirm people really care about this move?
- Is the gap happening across **the whole market** or just one stock?

Big gaps backed by real news and heavy volume are more likely to continue (Gap and Go). Small gaps on light volume are more likely to reverse and fill.

**The #1 Beginner Mistake With Gaps**

Seeing a stock gap down 10% and thinking "great deal, I'll buy the dip!" This is called catching a falling knife. Sometimes gaps keep going lower — especially when the news driving the gap is ongoing (like an escalating geopolitical conflict). Always wait for the stock to stabilize and show clear signs of reversing before entering.

**Today's Live Example to Watch**

The S&P 500 gapped down from Friday's close of 7,126 to roughly 7,110 this morning. Watch throughout today: Will the gap fill (prices recover back toward 7,126 by afternoon)? Or will Iran news keep escalating and push the gap lower? You're watching real gap trading unfold in real time — completely free.
lesson.key_takeaway: Gaps are when markets open at a very different price from their last close, caused by overnight news. You can ride the momentum (Gap and Go) or bet prices return to normal (Gap Fill) — but always confirm with volume and news quality, and never blindly buy a gap down just because it looks cheaper.

tips.trading_tip: On high-volatility, news-driven days like today, wait at least 30-60 minutes after the open before entering any trade. The first 30 minutes are the most chaotic — full of emotional overreactions, false moves, and stop-loss triggers. Let the dust settle, then trade with a clear head.
tips.risk_reminder: Iran-driven oil moves have reversed multiple times this month — the Strait opened, closed, then opened again. Don't chase oil stocks or energy ETFs at the open on geopolitical news. Wait for a clear, sustained trend to confirm before risking real money on volatile, news-driven moves.
tips.motivation: Today's market turbulence is a completely free classroom. You don't have to trade to learn — just watch. Watch the gap happen, watch the sectors rotate, watch how the market reacts when new Iran headlines drop. Every hour you spend observing without losing money is education that will eventually be worth real dollars.

disclaimer: This report is for educational and informational purposes only. It is NOT financial advice. Always do your own research before making any investment decisions. Day trading involves significant risk — never trade with money you can't afford to lose.
